question: Reference cohort
options: Ref A (109 pts, all with >=1 occ) | Ref B (52 pts, primary only) | No age
empirical_evidence: Ref A age range 8.69-16.75; Ref B age range 8.80-16.18; Ref B conditions on follow-up completeness (selection bias); age difference t-test p=0.952 (not significant)
caveat: Ref A includes single-occasion participants who did not return

question: Age-adjustment policy
caveat: Prespecified rule applied: M1 adopted if RMSE improvement >2%, slope p<0.10, across majority of tasks (>=3/5). Result: 0/5 tasks met all criteria. Global policy: M0_no_age_adjustment. Linear adjustment retained as sensitivity regardless.

question: Age-model form
options: M0 intercept-only | M1 linear | M2 spline df=3
caveat: M2 spline shows NO improvement over M1 and is prone to overfitting with N~10/fold. M2 is excluded from primary analysis.

question: Primary scale estimator
options: SD primary MAD sensitivity | MAD primary SD sensitivity
empirical_evidence: cnb_lnb_mcr: SD=2.816, MAD=1.631, ratio=1.777, skew=-1.958; cnb_cpf_cr: SD=4.345, MAD=4.744, ratio=0.927, skew=-0.359; cnb_pmat_cr: SD=4.529, MAD=2.965, ratio=1.527, skew=0.780; cnb_er40_cr: SD=4.495, MAD=2.965, ratio=1.516, skew=-1.817; cnb_ctap_dom: SD=7.824, MAD=7.314, ratio=1.070, skew=0.072
caveat: Prespecified rule: MAD primary only if SD/MAD ratio>1.3 AND heavy tail for >=3/5 tasks AND no near-zero MAD. Result: ratio>1.3 tasks=3/5, any near-zero MAD=False. Decision: MAD_primary_SD_sensitivity. Discrete count scores (LNB, CPF, PMAT, ER40) may produce compressed MAD.

question: Extrapolation algorithm
options: P1 flag+allow | P2 cap age | P3 use no-age coordinate | P4 refuse
empirical_evidence: 60 extrapolated task rows from 52 follow-up occasion rows (all 5 tasks). Unique extrapolated participants: 12. Unique (participant,task) combos: 60.
caveat: The 60 refers to task rows (not unique participants). Unique participants with >=1 extrapolated task: 12. P3 retains all participants in analyses.

question: Missingness policy
options: No imputation | Partial profiles in sensitivity
empirical_evidence: Primary cohort requires 5 tasks at both occasions

question: Extreme-observation policy
empirical_evidence: Winsorization not prespecified; extremes may be real

question: Transformation-uncertainty approach
empirical_evidence: 1000/1000 valid replicates (100.0%) over 1000 reps. Verdict: FEASIBLE. Reference A reconstructed inside each replicate. Age model and scale refitted.
caveat: Feasibility 100.0%. Step 5B target 5,000 valid reps from max 10,000 attempts. Fallback to fixed transformation if <95% valid.

question: Primary profile estimand
empirical_evidence: Level is transformationally simplest; shape requires good transformation quality

question: Secondary estimands
options: Centered shape | Scatter | Shape-change RMSE | Profile correlation
empirical_evidence: Centered shape components sum to 0 (4-dim subspace). Profile corr unstable k=5.
caveat: Five centered components are algebraically dependent (sum to zero, 4-dim).

question: Multiplicity policy
options: Bootstrap CI primary | Bonferroni | Uncorrected p-values
empirical_evidence: N=52 limits power; multiple estimands inflate false positive risk

question: SEM/MDC status
empirical_evidence: Long variable intervals violate static true-score assumption
caveat: Must carry caveat that assumes static true score, likely false in adolescents
